messages:
julia_customer: Hey team — started seeing a spike of users failing to login via Google/GitHub SSO. They hit our /auth/callback and we return 403 with 'state_mismatch'. No consistent pattern yet, sometimes works, sometimes not. Repro steps below.

maya_support: Sorry about that, can you paste a failed callback URL + any callback logs? Also which client (web/mobile) and browser?

julia_customer: Repro (one of the failing flows):
1) User clicks 'Sign in' (web) -> we redirect to provider with pkce & state
2) Provider redirects back to https://app.example.com/auth/callback?code=4/xxx&state=eyJhbGci...truncated
3) Our endpoint loads session cookie, compares state -> mismatch -> 403.

Sample redirect we captured:
https://app.example.com/auth/callback?code=4/AbcDef&state=eyJzdGF0ZSI6ImFiYy0xMjM0NTc%3D

Console log on our side: 
[auth] callback: incoming state=eyJzdGF0ZSI6ImFiYy0xMjM0NTc%3D, session.state=eyJzdGF0ZSI6ImFiYw
(note session.state seems truncated)

maya_support: Which deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)? Any proxies/load balancers in front?

julia_customer: Hosted. We sit behind our CDN + an edge proxy that rewrites some querystrings for analytics. Most fails are from Chrome mobile and iOS Safari webviews.

devon_engineer: Thanks. Two quick theories:
- state or pkce verifier getting truncated by either our cookie chunking or query rewriting (common with long base64 state).
- plus/space or percent encoding normalization at the edge (some proxies change '+' -> ' ').

Can you share the Set-Cookie header we use to persist the original state? Also paste the raw request headers from the failing callback if you have them.

julia_customer: Set-Cookie we set on /start-auth: 
Set-Cookie: sx_auth=eyJzdGF0ZSI6ImFiYy0xMjM0NTc%3D; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=None; HttpOnly

Failed callback headers: 
Cookie: sx_auth=eyJzdGF0ZSI6ImFiYw
Referer: https://accounts.google.com/
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 15_5 like Mac OS X)

maya_support: Cookie looks truncated in the request. That explains session.state shorter than incoming state param. Could be cookie chunking: large cookie got split and only first chunk sent. Do you split cookies on the app?

julia_customer: We don't intentionally split. Cookie size is ~320 bytes sometimes with extra metadata. Some users have cookies > 4kb due to long state+meta from some providers.

devon_engineer: Browsers only send a single Cookie header composed of name=value pairs and have per-cookie size limits (~4096 bytes). If any intermediary (edge CDN) strips cookies or drops long ones it can truncate the value. Also some older edge rules truncate query string segments > X length.

sre_bot: quickcheck: run a curl with the original Set-Cookie stored and then make the callback request. Example: 
curl -v -b "sx_auth=eyJzdGF0ZSI6ImFiYy0xMjM0NTc%3D" "https://app.example.com/auth/callback?code=...&state=eyJzdGF0ZSI6ImFiYy0xMjM0NTc%3D"

devon_engineer: Another gotcha: oauth state generated as base64 with '+' '/' '='. If edge or mobile deep link uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded normalization, '+' becomes space when not percent-encoded. Use urlsafe base64 or explicitly encode.

julia_customer: We saw a couple of callback URLs where state had '+' replaced by space in logs. Example failing state in callback: eyJzdGF0ZSI6ImFiYyA... (space char visible when logged raw)

ari_product: Is this affecting signup funnels badly? % drop?

julia_customer: ~4% of SSO attempts in last 24h failed with state_mismatch, a bump from ~0.2%. Most from mobile webviews + some corporate proxies.

devon_engineer: Quick mitigations:
- Short-term: add robust logging and a lenient retry path: if session.state is prefix-of incoming-state (or vice versa) log and attempt to re-run exchange after asking user to re-click sign-in (avoid silent auth loops).
- Medium: switch to storing opaque short state IDs (random 16 bytes hex) in cookie or DB and map to full meta server-side. Keeps cookie small.
- Long-term: switch to storing state in an HttpOnly signed cookie with minimal payload and verify server-side, or move to server-side session keyed by session cookie that is robust to chunking.

maya_support: Also audit edge rules that canonicalize querystrings. Ask CDN team: do we normalize + to space when forwarding?

julia_customer: I can open a ticket with CDN. For immediate repro we turned on debug in prod and captured two failing callbacks including raw tcp capture from edge (attached in ticket).

devon_engineer: For PKCE: verify code_verifier length. Some mobile SDKs shorten verifier or re-encode. If code_verifier stored in cookie and that cookie truncated, exchange will fail with 'invalid_grant' not state mismatch; so this looks cookie truncation for state specifically.

julia_customer: We also saw one case where callback had duplicate state param: ?state=abc&state=abc%20 -> our parser picked the first one which was truncated. Might want to normalize to last param.

ari_product: Let's treat as a P1 for auth reliability until mitigations deployed. Maya, can you own coordinating with CDN and escalate to infra?

maya_support: On it. I'll file infra ticket, include sample tcp dump + failing headers. Devon, can you draft a short fix plan for short opaque state IDs and a migration path?

devon_engineer: Will do. Draft plan: generate 16-byte hex state -> store mapping in redis with TTL 5m plus optional debug blob keyed by id. Update start-auth to set cookie with that id only. Validate at callback. Rollout with canary and monitor state_mismatch rate.

julia_customer: Thanks. One more note: a subset of failures were from our Android webview wrapper that strips url fragment and rewrites query by decoding twice. We should add instrumentation to detect double-decoding.

maya_support: Action items summarized:
- infra: check CDN querystring normalization and cookie size forwarding (maya).
- eng: implement short opaque state id + redis mapping (devon).
- support: add heuristic logging + retry UX for affected users (maya/julia).
- product: declare P1 and notify comms if user-facing (ari).

deploy_bot: deploy scheduled: staging canary for state-id change at 2026-03-19T02:00Z.

julia_customer: repro steps and logs are in the ticket. I'll monitor funnel and post updates here. :thumbsup:

maya_support: Thanks everyone — will update with CDN findings and a link to the infra ticket shortly. :eyes:
